stage_note: No source we have read names this parcel in an approval.
summary: Planned quieter park at the south-east tip of the site, set apart from Block 9's more social uses: natural planted areas, informal discovery play, and casual seating and picnicking, with a Bay overlook on the footprint of a decommissioned power plant intake structure and a section of Blue Greenway for a future connection toward Warm Water Cove, to be completed by others (Design for Development Section 4.20). The Power Station website calls it a place set 'at the tip of the site'.

facts.value: picnic areas with picnic tables and benches, discovery play features, seating, lighting, outdoor grills, and waste receptacles (D4D 4.20.3)

open_questions: No source read gives The Point's acreage or a construction date.

The Design for Development's own outline of The Point (Figure 4.20.1) has not been georeferenced; the shape on the map was traced from satellite imagery, and it also takes in the shoreline strip and the pier-like structure at the end of 23rd Street that appears to be the decommissioned intake structure the D4D says the Bay overlook is to be built on. That reading is Pier & Point's.
The earlier Waterfront Park drawing included part of this ground; the Power Station website describes The Point as set 'at the tip of the site' but gives no boundary.
